identity.name: Carnauba wax
identity.chemical_class: Natural plant wax composed mainly of long-chain aliphatic esters, fatty acids, and fatty alcohols

function.mechanism: Forms a hard, hydrophobic surface film that improves gloss and acts as a moisture/physical barrier; also supports processing via anti-caking and release effects.

adi.basis: EFSA 2012 re-evaluation of E903 reported ADI 7 mg/kg bw/day and concluded no safety concern at reported uses/exposure.

efsa.key_finding: Latest located EFSA opinion is the 2012 re-evaluation; indexed summary text reports low absorption/partial hydrolysis and no safety concern at reported use levels.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI is listed as 0-7 mg/kg bw (chemical entry for CARNAUBA WAX).

concerns.summary: Modern, additive-specific long-term human safety datasets are limited; core toxicology evidence remains largely historical animal feeding studies.

A formulation-specific oral nanoparticle study (carnauba-wax SLN loaded with rosmarinic acid) reported safe findings at moderate concentrations but in vitro genotoxic potential at higher test concentration; relevance to typical E903 dietary exposure is indirect.

no_concern_confirmed: Rat and beagle dog feeding studies (1982-1983) did not show clear treatment-related toxicity/pathology at tested dietary concentrations, including up to 10% diet in short-term rat study.
Regulatory consensus across EFSA, FDA (CFR), and JECFA supports controlled use with established ADI/GMP frameworks.
No specific IARC carcinogenic classification entry for carnauba wax was found in the current IARC classification dataset checked.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA re-evaluation summary text indicates mean and high-level exposure estimates were below ADI across evaluated population groups/scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E903 is approved by major regulators, has consistent ADIs (EFSA 7; JECFA 0-7 mg/kg bw/day), and has no IARC classification signal identified. The main uncertainty is that much of the direct toxicology base is older and modern additive-specific human data are limited.
key_factors: EFSA 2012 re-evaluation with ADI 7 mg/kg bw/day and no safety concern conclusion
U.S. GRAS affirmation and GMP-limited conditions in 21 CFR 184.1978
JECFA ADI 0-7 mg/kg bw (1992 evaluation record)
Historical animal studies without major treatment-related toxicity
No carnauba wax entry found in IARC classifications dataset
